title: This day in history: Ida Caldwell McFaddin was born in 1872 - NewsBreak
text:
By Megan Zapalac ,
10 hours ago Ida Cadlwell McFaddin, one of the original McFaddiN-Ward House owners. (Courtesy of the Bullock Museum) One of the original McFaddin-Ward House owners, Ida Caldwell McFaddin was born on this day in 1872.
Born on Sept. 24, 1872, McFaddin was the daughter of a prominent family in Huntington, West Virginia. She married William Perry McFaddin Sr. in 1894, according to the McFaddin-Ward House Museum website.
She was a social and civic leader in Beaumont during the 1910s and 20s who had two sons, William Perry McFaddin Jr. and James Lewis Caldwell McFaddin, along with one daughter, Mamie McFaddin Ward, the museum said.
Between 1905 and 1906, McFaddin and William Perry Sr. built their historic home, which is now a museum at 1906 McFaddin Ave. After her brother died, McFaddin served as president of her family’s company in Huntington, the Caldwell Company, according to the museum.
RELATED: This day in history: Gregory Fleniken dies after shot through Elegante wall
McFaddin also served on the board of the Beaumont Children’s Home and was very active in the Daughters of the American Revolution. Through her work, she donated land to start the Daughters of the American Revolution State Forest in Jasper, according to the Texas State Historical Association.
She also served as local and state regent of the Daughters of the American Revolution and president general of the national society. She was active in the National Society of Colonial Dames and other “patriotic” organizations, the historical association said.
As a philanthropist, McFaddin supported the United Charities, the YWCA, the Beaumont Children's Home and Lamar College, now Lamar University, according to the historical association.
She was also active in the Episcopal Church, serving as a guild member and Sunday school teacher, along with singing in the choir, according to the Bullock Museum website.
McFaddin died in Beaumont on March 21, 1950.
